title: Multi-view attention-based deep learning for benign-malignant classification of pulmonary nodules.
abstract: Accurate classification of pulmonary nodules is essential for early lung cancer diagnosis, yet the limited spatial information provided by a single computed tomography slice may hinder the characterization of complex nodule morphology. Although multi-view strategies can capture complementary anatomical information, conventional fusion methods often fail to account for lesion-specific features and differences in the contribution of individual views. To address these limitations, we propose a tri-view pulmonary nodule classification framework that combines Lesion-Guided Attention (LGA) with View-Weighted Fusion (VWF). The framework extracts complementary representations from axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. LGA introduces lesion masks as weak spatial priors to refine lesion-related feature responses while preserving contextual information, whereas VWF learns sample-dependent weights to adaptively aggregate the three view representations. The framework was evaluated on 869 nodules (448 benign and 421 malignant) derived from the public Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. It achieved an accuracy of 93.08%, an AUC of 97.06%, and an F1-score of 92.68%, representing the highest values for these three metrics among the models included in the baseline comparison. Ablation analysis further showed that the combined use of LGA and VWF provided the best overall balance among the evaluated configurations. In the displayed test cases, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping visualizations showed that the learned responses were concentrated mainly within or adjacent to lesion-relevant regions. These findings support the potential value of combining lesion-aware feature refinement with adaptive multi-view fusion for pulmonary nodule classification within the evaluated LIDC-IDRI cohort.

title: Impact of dual-layer spectral CT-derived stopping power ratio on single-energy CT-based carbon-ion treatment planning for thoracic cancer.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the impact of stopping-power ratio (SPR) predictions derived from dual-layer detector-based spectral CT (DLCT) on conventional single-energy CT (SECT)-based carbon-ion treatment planning for thoracic cancer. Methods Twenty patients with thoracic cancer who underwent non-contrast DLCT were retrospectively included. DLCT-based SPR images were generated from effective atomic number and relative electron density maps using the Bethe equation. SECT-based SPR was derived using a Hounsfield unit look-up table generated via stoichiometric calibration of a commercial electron density phantom. Using the same phantom, a phantom-based prediction assessment was performed by comparing SECT- and DLCT-based SPR predictions with theoretical SPR values for the inserts. For patient analysis, normal-tissue SPR values derived from SECT and DLCT were compared. Carbon-ion treatment plans were first generated based on SECT images and then recalculated using DLCT-derived SPR images. Range differences in the beam's-eye view and dose-volume histogram parameters for the planning target volume and organs at risk were evaluated. Results In the phantom-based assessment, the root-mean-square error relative to the theoretical SPR was 5.57% for SECT and 2.83% for DLCT. In patient images, mean SPR differences between SECT and DLCT were 3.62% for the lungs, 1.93% for the esophagus, 0.04% for the heart, 0.93% for the spinal cord, and 1.53% for the ribs. Across the patient cohort, the mean recalculated range difference was 0.71 ± 0.89 mm, corresponding to a relative difference of 0.60 ± 0.67%. No statistically significant differences were observed in target dose metrics, whereas selected organ-at-risk metrics showed statistically significant differences between SECT-based plans and DLCT-based recalculations. Conclusion DLCT-derived SPR prediction showed better agreement with theoretical phantom SPR values in the phantom-based prediction assessment and produced tissue-dependent SPR differences in thoracic patient images compared with conventional SECT-based prediction. Recalculation on DLCT-derived SPR maps resulted in modest but systematic range differences and limited changes in selected dose metrics. These results may inform the implementation and future independent validation of patient-specific DLCT-based SPR workflows in carbon-ion treatment planning for thoracic cancer.

title: Not All Pancreatic Masses are Cancer: Pancreatic Tuberculosis Masquerading as Malignancy.
abstract: Pancreatic tuberculosis (TB) is a rare extrapulmonary manifestation that can mimic pancreatic cancer. We report a 61-year-old man presenting with epigastric discomfort, weight loss, elevated liver enzymes, elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9, and a pancreatic mass causing biliary obstruction. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsies revealed granulomatous inflammation and necrosis. Autoimmune and fungal etiologies were excluded, and acid-fast stains were negative. Definitive diagnosis was achieved through 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing followed by detection of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis hsp65 gene. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of pancreatic TB and the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when histopathological findings do not align with clinical suspicion.

title: Five Novel Sonographic Signs
abstract: Ultrasound is a widely used imaging modality in clinical practice, and sonographic signs serve as valuable teaching tools that aid in pattern recognition and diagnosis. This review consolidates five novel sonographic signs previously proposed by the author, including the Cracked Earth Sign for subcutaneous edema, the Mushroom Cap Sign for localized gallbladder adenomyomatosis, the LTS Sign for dilated cardiomyopathy, the LTI Sign for endocardial fibroelastosis, and the Three Pipes Sign for the suprasternal long-axis view of the aortic arch, spanning the fields of superficial ultrasound, abdominal ultrasound, and echocardiography. For each sign, its naming logic, definition, clinical implications, and teaching value are described. This review aims to facilitate a better understanding of these signs and to promote their use as teaching aids in ultrasound education.

title: Classification of Forearm Involvement in Multiple Hereditary Exostoses: Consensus from the CoULD Study Group.
abstract: Background Existing classifications for forearm deformity in multiple hereditary exostoses (MHE) have demonstrated low interrater reliability and limited clinical applicability. Our primary research question was whether a Delphi consensus process could generate a more reliable and clinically useful classification for longitudinal surveillance of MHE-related forearm deformities. Methods Fifteen pediatric hand surgeons from the Congenital Upper Limb Difference (CoULD) Study Group participated in 7 rounds of online Delphi surveys (June 2022 to September 2023). An investigator team facilitated the process with anonymized feedback. Round 1 identified key clinical and radiographic features. Subsequent rounds refined these features, determined categorical structure, and piloted the system with representative radiographs. Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement. After final consensus, interrater reliability was tested by 4 independent surgeons who classified 101 radiographs from 67 patients with forearm MHE. Reliability was assessed with kappa and concordance coefficients and compared with the Masada, Gottschalk, and Jo classifications. Results The Delphi process identified radiographic predictors that included ulnar variance, the radial articular angle (RAA), radial head alignment, and osteochondroma size. Consensus favored a 3-tier classification: Type 1, mild; Type 2, moderate; and Type 3, severe. Closing consensus was achieved, with 93% agreement. Reliability testing showed moderate agreement on the first reading (kappa = 0.55), significantly higher than for the Masada (kappa = 0.21 [original classification], kappa = 0.35 [modified version]), Gottschalk (kappa = 0.43), and Jo (kappa = 0.43) classifications. After refinement that incorporated osteochondroma size and the radial head subtypes (3A, subluxation, and 3B, dislocation), agreement improved to substantial (kappa = 0.64) (p < 0.001), with high concordance (0.82). Conclusions The CoULD MHE Classification, developed through expert consensus, integrates validated radiographic predictors with defined thresholds. It demonstrated significantly improved reliability over prior systems and provides a practical framework for longitudinal monitoring of forearm deformities in patients with MHE. Level of evidence Diagnostic Level V. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Biopsies from Normal-Appearing Mucosa in Pediatric Upper GI Endoscopy: What Do They Tell Us?
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Histopathological abnormalities may be detected despite normal endoscopic findings in pediatric upper gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy. However, the clinical value of routine biopsies from macroscopically normal mucosa remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the impact of such biopsies on diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of children undergoing upper GI endoscopy at a tertiary care center over a one-year period. Biopsies obtained from macroscopically normal esophageal, gastric, and duodenal mucosa were analyzed. Biopsy findings were assessed for their impact on clinical management, defined as any change in treatment or follow-up. Results were evaluated according to both the number of affected patients and the total number of biopsy specimens. Results: A total of 802 endoscopies were included. Biopsies from normal-appearing mucosa were obtained in 577 patients (71.9%), yielding 2,055 biopsy specimens. Histopathological findings altered clinical management in 60 patients (10.4%). At the biopsy level, 116 specimens (5.6%) revealed clinically relevant findings, whereas 542 (26.4%) showed inflammatory changes without clinical impact and 1,397 (68.0%) were histologically normal. Most management-changing findings were related to Helicobacter pylori infection (26/60). Clinical impact varied according to presenting symptoms and biopsy site. Conclusions: Routine biopsy of macroscopically normal mucosa during pediatric upper GI endoscopy rarely influences clinical management. A selective biopsy strategy guided by presenting symptoms, clinical suspicion, and established guideline recommendations may optimize diagnostic yield while reducing unnecessary procedures.

title: Prediction of LN-prRLN Metastasis in cN0 PTMC Patients Using Logistic Regression and Machine Learning: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background The incidence of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC) is steadily increasing, with metastasis to lymph nodes posterior to the right recurrent laryngeal nerve (LN-prRLN) occurring in 7.1% to 34.9% of cases. Preoperative ultrasound fails to detect most LN-prRLN metastases. Accurate risk assessment of LN-prRLN in clinically node-negative (cN0) PTMC patients is essential for determining the appropriate surgical extent and evaluating the feasibility of active surveillance. Objective To develop and compare logistic regression and machine learning models for predicting LN-prRLN metastasis in cN0 PTMC patients, thereby supporting individualized preoperative and intraoperative clinical decision-making. Methods A total of 1051 cN0 PTMC patients were retrospectively analyzed and randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Clinical, ultrasonographic, and pathological variables were collected. Using LN-prRLN metastasis status as the endpoint, logistic regression and multiple machine learning models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), calibration curves, and precision-recall curves. The best-performing machine learning model was compared with the logistic model, and SHAP values were employed for model interpretability. Results Multivariate logistic regression identified anterior prelaryngeal lymph node metastatic ratio (LNMR) and anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve LNMR as independent predictors of LN-prRLN metastasis. Among machine learning algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the best discriminative ability and calibration stability. Although XGBoost yielded higher area under the ROC curve (AUC) values than the logistic model in both training and validation sets, the difference was not statistically significant. SHAP analysis revealed that anterior prelaryngeal LNMR and anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve LNMR were the two most influential predictors, contributing cumulatively over 66% to the prediction with strong interaction effects. Other notable contributors included anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve lymph node metastasis, prelaryngeal lymph node metastasis, tumor size, left central compartment LNMR, capsular invasion, age, left central compartment lymph node metastasis, and multifocality. Conclusion Both logistic regression and machine learning models are reliable tools for predicting LN-prRLN metastasis in cN0 PTMC patients. Integrating these models can assist clinicians in accurately identifying high-risk patients preoperatively or intraoperatively, enabling more patient-centered clinical decisions.

title: Application of CT-Based Three-Dimensional Reconstruction to Guide Anatomical Resection for Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformations in Children
abstract: Abstract Purpose To describe CT-based patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction for lesion-oriented anatomical regional resection and compare the short-term outcomes of three surgical approaches for pediatric congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM). Methods We retrospectively reviewed 185 children treated between July 2023 and March 2025: segmentectomy (n=62), lobectomy (n=66), and anatomical regional resection (n=57). Noncontrast thin-slice CT data were reconstructed using Mimics to delineate the lesion, bronchi, pulmonary arteries, and pulmonary veins. Perioperative outcomes and postoperative complications were compared among the groups. Results Age and weight did not differ significantly among the groups. Operative times were 95±5.9, 80±3.7, and 92±5.7 min, while chest tube durations were 4±1.3, 2±1.1, and 2±1.4 days, respectively (both overall P<0.001). Pneumothorax, subcutaneous emphysema, pneumonia, and localized atelectasis did not differ significantly. Radiographic compensatory pulmonary hyperinflation occurred in 2, 10, and 1 children, respectively (overall P=0.009). Conclusion Patient-specific 3D reconstruction provided an anatomically explicit basis for lesion-oriented operative planning. Anatomical regional resection was feasible; however, the observed between-group differences require cautious interpretation because treatment allocation was nonrandomized. Prospective multicenter studies with adjusted analyses and standardized imaging follow-up are warranted.

title: Gut Check! Effectiveness of Emergency Room Investigations for Acute Appendicitis
abstract: Abstract Purpose Ultrasound (US) is the most used imaging modality in children with suspected appendicitis, with high sensitivity and diagnostic accuracy. Our institution utilizes a standardized US findings reporting system evaluating for appendicitis, which may obviate the need for CT scan if findings are consistent with appendicitis. In this study, we aimed to characterize the efficacy of our protocol for emergency room appendicitis workup and identify any risk factors contributing to a missed diagnosis. We hypothesize that < 10% of patients who underwent appendectomy presented within the preceding 14 days with symptoms of abdominal pain and our current investigative framework failed to identify acute appendicitis. Methods We conducted a single institution retrospective review of all pediatric patients who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy from 2020 to 2022 to determine the rates of prior presentation to the emergency department with a negative workup for acute appendicitis in the 14 days prior to formal diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Demographics and clinical characteristics were collected. Differences between groups were compared by using the Fisher’s Exact Test or Chi-Square test for categorical variables. Results A total of 1902 patients met inclusion criteria with a median age of 11.4 years (IQR 8.3, 14.4). Most patients were male (N = 1,094, 58%), white (N = 1,244, 65%), English speaking (N = 1,695, 89%) Sixty-two patients (3.3%) were seen in the emergency department for abdominal pain within 14 days prior to appendicitis diagnosis, and an additional six patients (0.3%) were seen within the prior 30 days. These patients were younger with a median age of 7.4 years (N = 4, 12.5%) (p = < 0.001) and more likely to be non-English speaking (N = 17, 27%) (p = < 0.001). Thirteen (21%) patients had an ultrasound at initial presentation, and an additional three (5%) had a CT scan. Ultrasound findings included: Category 1 (N = 2), Category 2 (N = 5), indeterminate (N = 1), free fluid (N = 1), dilated appendix (N = 1). At the time of discharge on initial presentation, these patients were diagnosed with constipation (N = 7), abdominal pain (N = 22), gastroenteritis (N = 14), and other (N = 10). Surgery was consulted on 8% (N = 5) of these cases. Missed appendicitis patients had a higher rate of perforation (45.2% vs 27.7%, p < 0.001) and longer mean length of stay (56 hrs vs 9 hrs, p < 0.001). Conclusion Patients who presented with acute appendicitis after an initial missed diagnosis are more likely to have perforation and longer inpatient LOS. While a protocolized emergency room diagnostic workup for appendicitis is effective, barriers to effective communication with patients may contribute to missed diagnosis and should be considered in clinical decision making.

title: Cross-cohort evaluation of thyroid ultrasound deep learning across different outcome definitions: a duplicate-controlled benchmark
abstract: Abstract Background. Measured performance of thyroid ultrasound artificial intelligence depends on both cohort characteristics and the evaluation endpoint. We assessed frozen models across public cohorts with differing label provenance, separating evaluation against malignancy outcomes from agreement with ultrasound risk categories. Methods. Five backbones were trained on 387 thyroid ultrasound images from 385 public cases (222 papillary thyroid carcinoma, 163 benign) labelled by postoperative diagnosis; 1,332 fine-needle aspiration cytology blocks from the same archive formed a separate benchmark. Exact and perceptual near-duplicates were grouped before image-level partitioning; per-image patient identifiers were unavailable, so patient-level independence could not be confirmed. Frozen models were evaluated on a TN3K subset (n = 1,228; dataset-provided benign/malignant labels) and for concordance with an endpoint derived from radiologist Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS) categories in DDTI (n = 637), without retraining or threshold adjustment. Results. On TN3K the ensemble reached an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.825 (95% confidence interval 0.800–0.849) and ResNet-50 reached 0.888 (0.870–0.904). Against the TI-RADS-derived endpoint, AUROC was 0.477 and 0.437, indicating little agreement with that categorisation. Because cohort, acquisition and endpoint changed together, this contrast cannot be attributed to label definition alone. The cytology benchmark reached AUROC 0.986 (0.970–0.998) against 0.733 for the ultrasound ensemble, a descriptive non-paired contrast. Conclusions. Frozen models performed differently across cohorts differing in acquisition and outcome definition. The findings support explicit reporting of label provenance, cautious interpretation of cross-cohort contrasts, and patient-level external evaluation against a clinically appropriate reference standard.

title: Comparative detection performance of different imaging modalities in suspected cardiac sarcoidosis: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Background The optimal imaging modality for detecting cardiac sarcoidosis remains uncertain, since direct comparative data are largely limited to single tracer pairs. The aim of the present study was to estimate and rank the diagnostic detection performance of positron emission tomography (PET), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and conventional scintigraphy modalities in suspected cardiac sarcoidosis through a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA). Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to June 2026 for studies directly comparing at least two imaging modalities. A frequentist random-effect NMA was conducted with detection rate (DR) as primary outcome, 18 F-FDG PET/CT as reference, and effect sizes expressed as risk differences (RDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Node-splitting and sensitivity analyses were applied to assess consistency and rank stability. Results Ten studies (n = 430 patients or lesions) met inclusion criteria, forming a network of nine modalities. CMR with late gadolinium enhancement (CMR-LGE) yielded the highest DR (RD 0.18 versus 18 F-FDG PET/CT; 95% CI, 0.11 to 0.25), followed by 68 Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT (RD 0.11; 95% CI, − 0.09 to 0.30); 18 F-FLT PET/CT was essentially equivalent to the reference (RD 0.00; 95% CI, − 0.23 to 0.24). 67 Ga scintigraphy yielded the lowest DR (RD − 0.73; 95% CI, − 0.82 to − 0.65). Four modalities differed significantly from 18 F-FDG PET/CT (CMR-LGE above the reference, and 67 Ga scintigraphy, 99m Tc-MIBI SPECT, and T2w-CMR below). Conclusion Our findings suggest that CMR-LGE and 68 Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT may yield a higher DR than 18 F-FDG PET/CT, while conventional radionuclide techniques appear comparatively limited. Trial registration: INPLASY (INPLASY202630093)

title: Evaluation of CBCT-based HU correction for synthetic CT generation in head-and-neck radiotherapy: FOV-stratified and peripheral-region analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is essential for image-guided radiotherapy for head and neck (H&N) cancer but suffers from inaccurate Hounsfield units (HUs) due to scatter, artifacts, and field of view (FOV) truncation, limiting its use for dose calculation. We aimed to compare linear correction, a residual U-Net model (ResUNet), and a paired cycle-consistent conditional GAN (PCC-cGAN) framework with residual U-Net generators for HU correction and synthetic CT (sCT) generation, the deep learning models trained in a paired setting, with the CycleGAN variant adapted from its original unpaired design to exploit cycle-consistency in addition to supervised training. Our evaluation emphasizes FOV stratification (complete vs. truncated) and spatial localization of residual errors. This study provides an FOV-stratified and peripheral-aware evaluation of CBCT-based HU correction, highlighting residual error patterns that may be overlooked by global MAE analysis alone. Methods A total of 100 CBCT/CT pairs from 67 H&N patients were divided into complete FOV (19 pairs) and truncated FOV (81 pairs) groups. Evaluation was performed within three spatial mask regions: intersection, eroded intersection, and peripheral. An independent-patient sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess patient‑level overlap. Preliminary body‑level dosimetric consistency was evaluated by comparing raw CBCT and ResUNet sCT against the reference planning CT (pCT) dose using gamma pass rates (2%/2mm and 3%/3mm) and dose Mean Absolute Error & Root Mean Squared Error (MAE/RMSE). Results ResUNet achieved the lowest HU-MAE across the evaluated regions in both FOV groups. In the independent-patient subset, this pattern was preserved for intersection and eroded mask regions, with ResUNet performing best in nearly all of the patient-region combinations. The peripheral MAE remained substantially higher than the intersection and eroded MAE for all methods (e.g., ResUNet: 171.51 vs. 76.93 HU in the complete FOV). Body‑level gamma pass rates (GPR) and dose metrics were generally maintained or modestly improved by ResUNet, but HU improvements did not translate proportionally to dosimetric gains across all patients. Conclusions ResUNet provided the lowest HU-MAE among the evaluated methods under the conditions of this study for CBCT-based sCT generation in H&N radiotherapy, with persistent residual errors concentrated at the peripheral evaluation region, where the highest residual MAE was observed. The FOV-stratified and peripheral-aware evaluation framework introduced here informs future DVH-based validation and dose-of-the-day adaptive workflows.

title: Adenocarcinoma of the Minor Duodenal Papilla Mimicking a Pancreatic Head Tumor: A Rare Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background Adenocarcinoma of the minor duodenal papilla (papilla of Santorini) is an exceptionally rare periampullary malignancy, with only a small number of cases reported in the literature. Its close anatomical relationship with the pancreatic head and duodenum can make determination of the primary site difficult, particularly after local invasion. Case presentation: A 72-year-old woman presented with progressive dysphagia, early satiety, epigastric pain, vomiting, and significant weight loss. Endoscopy demonstrated stenosis of the second portion of the duodenum, while computed tomography and endoscopic ultrasonography revealed an approximately 3-cm lesion in the pancreatic-head/uncinate region. Neither the common bile duct nor the main pancreatic duct was dilated, and the patient had no clinical or biochemical evidence of obstructive jaundice. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19 − 9 was markedly elevated at 7,619 U/mL. Following preoperative optimization, pancreaticoduodenectomy was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated adenocarcinoma centered on the minor duodenal papilla, extending through the duodenal wall and superficially invading the pancreas, while the major papilla and common bile duct remained uninvolved. Surgical margins were negative, perineural invasion was present, and all 12 examined lymph nodes were negative for metastatic disease. The pathological stage was reported as pT3N0M0. Conclusion Minor duodenal papilla adenocarcinoma may mimic a pancreatic-head malignancy and can progress without biliary obstruction because of its anatomical separation from the common bile duct. Local invasion may further obscure its site of origin, potentially contributing to underrecognition among tumors classified as pancreatic or periampullary adenocarcinomas. Careful correlation of radiological, endoscopic, operative, and histopathological findings is therefore essential for accurate diagnosis.

Local invasion may further obscure its site of origin, potentially contributing to underrecognition among tumors classified as pancreatic or periampullary adenocarcinomas. Careful correlation of radiological, endoscopic, operative, and histopathological findings is therefore essential for accurate diagnosis.

title: Medical Artificial Intelligence: A Multimodal, Human-Centered, Domain-Adaptive Framework for Surgical Decision Support and Patient Safety
abstract: Abstract Background Surgical decision-making is complex, time-sensitive, and dependent on heterogeneous clinical information. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been investigated for risk prediction, medical imaging, intraoperative video analysis, and clinical decision support, but translation from model development to safe clinical use remains limited by generalizability, uncertainty, human-factors, and governance challenges. Methods We developed an evidence-informed conceptual framework for multimodal surgical decision support. A targeted literature synthesis was performed using peer-reviewed and regulatory sources published from 2020 through 28 August 2026, with emphasis on surgical AI, clinical prediction, multimodal systems, human-AI interaction, explainability, patient safety, validation, and AI governance. The framework specifies intended use, input modalities, modular AI architecture, domain adaptation, uncertainty estimation, safety controls, clinician interaction, validation stages, post-deployment monitoring, and regulatory lifecycle requirements. No patient-level dataset was analyzed, no model was trained, and no new clinical performance estimates were generated. Results The framework defines a traceable pipeline from multimodal clinical data to clinician-reviewed decision support and explicitly separates proposed architecture from evidence reported in the literature. Literature-derived evidence demonstrates substantial potential for surgical AI but also identifies important validation gaps. In a 36-study scoping review of AI-enabled surgical decision support, 80.6% of studies used internal validation only, 13.8% used external validation, and 5.6% used real-time validation; none evaluated clinical implementation efficacy. A 2024 systematic review of 102 clinically validated surgical AI studies similarly reported heterogeneous validation quality. These findings support staged validation rather than universal performance claims. No prospective clinical efficacy claim is made in the present framework. Conclusion A domain-adaptive, multimodal architecture can organize future surgical AI development around safety, transparency, human oversight, and reproducibility. Clinical effectiveness remains to be established through task-specific development, temporal and external validation, silent prospective deployment, human-AI evaluation, and prospective clinical studies.

title: Elevated S100B Levels Are Associated with Early Coagulation Disturbances in the Prehospital Phase of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: An Experimental Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) following severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) substantially contributes to secondary intracranial haemorrhage and mortality. sTBI confirmed by elevated blood-based neurobiomarkers, including S100B is associated with functional and dynamic coagulation abnormalities. Previous studies demonstrated that thromboelastometry-guided haemostatic management showed benefits through in-hospital management of trauma-associated intracranial bleedings; however, the initial stages of TIC in the prehospital phase remain insufficiently characterised. We hypothesized that the selective coagulation factor deficiency underlying sTBI-associated coagulopathy, potentially amplified by immune-mediated proinflammatory mechanisms, could be identified already in the prehospital phase. Methods A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted at three prehospital ambulance stations in Hungary. Adult patients with suspected sTBI, based on the overall prehospital clinical presentation — including GCS ≤8, suspected intracranial hemorrhage and/or the need for intensive care — were included. Prehospital blood samples were obtained prior to tranexamic acid administration for thromboelastometry (ROTEM ® ) and measurement of serum total calcium, S100B, and IL-6 concentrations. Results From the rotational thromboelastometry parameters FIBTEM A5 fell below the critical threshold of 9 mm in 7 of 12 patients (58.3%), with a median of 8 mm (IQR: 5.8–10.0 mm), indicating impaired fibrinogen-dependent clot formation. EXTEM clotting time exceeded the upper reference limit in 3 of 13 patients (23.1%). The median EXTEM A5 was 41 mm (IQR: 36–46), at the lower reference limit. Serum S100B concentrations were markedly elevated (median: 4.84 μg/L, IQR: 1.88–9.56) and correlated significantly with Marshall CT classification (r = 0.706, p = 0.010). The total serum calcium concentration trended towards the lower limit of the reference range (median: 2.26 mmol/L, IQR: 2.20–2.31). IL-6 levels were markedly elevated (median: 22.9 pg/mL, IQR: 6.2–65.3) and did not significantly correlate with EXTEM clotting time (r = 0.51, p = 0.074). Conclusions Selective fibrinogen-dependent coagulation impairment is detectable in the hyperacute prehospital phase of sTBI, prior to any resuscitative intervention, and may be linked to an early immune-mediated proinflammatory response. These findings support early prehospital fibrinogen supplementation and tranexamic acid therapy. The marked prehospital elevation of S100B, which correlates with intracranial injury severity, confirms its value as an early diagnostic biomarker of sTBI. Trial registration : Not applicable.

title: Why Variance Metrics Cannot Validate ComBat Harmonization: Evidence from Three-Vendor Mammography Radiomics
abstract: Abstract ComBat is the standard method for removing scanner- and vendor-related variation from radiomic features, yet its success is conventionally judged by variance statistics (ICC, η², Kruskal-Wallis) that ComBat aligns by construction, making such validation nearly tautological. Using expert tumor segmentations from three mammography vendors (n=120; analysis subset n=91) and 59 standardized features, we tested ComBat with evidence independent of the moments it targets. After harmonization a linear classifier could no longer identify the vendor (AUC 0.56) but a leakage-free random forest identified it perfectly (AUC 1.00), and inter-vendor covariance structure persisted (0.259→0.244). Naive ComBat also erased a batch-correlated biological covariate, tumor size (p=4.0×10⁻⁸→0.10), which covariate-protected ComBat preserved. Variance-based reporting may therefore give false assurance of cross-vendor comparability. Harmonization adequacy should therefore be certified by independent non-linear separability rather than by the variance statistics ComBat directly targets.

title: Eliminating False-Negative Discharges in Tuberculosis Screening: Multi-Cohort Development and Independent External Stress-Testing of an Auditable Conformal AI Safety Architecture
abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning tuberculosis triage risks silent false negatives from uncalibrated overconfidence, while benchmark AUROCs frequently reflect institutional artifacts. We evaluated an edge-deployable AI framework coupling DenseNet-121 with pre-analytic Input Quality Assurance (IQA), temperature scaling, Mondrian conformal prediction, and HiResCAM attribution. Methods We curated 12,599 radiographs across five institutions for development (training n=8,819, validation n=1,261, calibration n=1,261, test n=1,258), calibrating Mondrian bounds (α=0.05). The frozen 28.5 MB model was evaluated across 3,441 unseen external radiographs from rural secondary care (Solan, India; n=155), tertiary referral (NITRD New Delhi; n=278), and web-compressed imaging (Pakistan; n=3,008). Findings Across external Indian cohorts (n=433), the frozen model achieved AUROC 0.8613 (Solan rural CR, n=155; sensitivity 70.51%, specificity 87.01%) and AUROC 0.8721 (NITRD tertiary DR, n=278; sensitivity 78.40%, specificity 80.39%), pooling to AUROC 0.8682. On the internal test set (n=1,258, AUROC 0.9943), linear probe auditing revealed institutional acquisition shortcuts (Belarus cavitary TB vs RSNA normal controls, r=+0.7205). Noise retraining rescued Pakistan scans (AUROC 0.4982 to 0.7098) but degraded clean clinical scans (-0.20 AUROC drop). Crucially, while raw classifier sensitivities were 70.51% to 78.40%, assistive IQA and Mahalanobis interlocks eliminated autonomous false-negative discharges (0.00% autonomous discharge error, 0/203 active cases cleared without clinician review). Decision curve analysis demonstrated +14.07 net true positives per 1,000 cases and reduced unnecessary GeneXpert assays by 78.7%. The offline microservice operates with zero cloud cost, 348 MiB RAM, and 38.2 ms GPU latency (104 ms CPU). Interpretation Autonomous clearance is hazardous under sensor shift. By deferring indeterminate presentations to clinicians, conformal triage interlocks eliminate unreviewed false-negative discharges without feature distortion, providing a failsafe tool for resource-constrained clinics. Funding Independent departmental resources; no commercial funding.

title: Comparison of clinical and pathological characteristics between localized giant cell and fibroadenoma of tendon sheath
abstract: Abstract Objective: To explore the clinical and pathological characteristics of localized giant cell tumor of tendon sheath (L-GCTS) and fibroma of tendon sheath (FTS), and to compare and analyze them. Methods: 241 cases of L-GCTS and 41 cases of FTS who underwent surgical resection and diagnosis at Wuxi Ninth People's Hospital from 2019 to 2023 were collected. Clinical and pathological data of all cases were organized for retrospective analysis. Chi-square test was used to analyze differences between groups. Results: Comparing our two groups of cases, we found that L-GCTS is more common, while FTS is less common. However, the two were very similar in clinical features, disease course, age of onset, tumor size and overall appearance, as well as imaging manifestations; In our case, L-GCTS was more common in female patients, and there was no significant gender difference in FTS; L-GCTS was more common in the right hand, FTS was also more common in the hand, but the left incidence rate is slightly higher than the right, with no significant difference; In addition, a small number of L-GCTS were accompanied by damage to surrounding tissues, and 41 cases of FTS did not cause damage to surrounding tissues; L-GCTS and FTS are mostly single lesions, with a few being multiple lesions; Among 241 cases of L-GCTS, 235 were primary cases, 6 were recurrent cases, and 41 cases of FTS were all primary cases; The coincidence rate between preoperative imaging diagnosis and postoperative pathological diagnosis of L-GCTS was 89%, and the coincidence rate between preoperative imaging diagnosis and postoperative pathological diagnosis of FTS was 55.3%. The main reason was that it is easier to misdiagnose FTS as L-GCTS before surgery; There were certain differences in pathological and immunohistochemical manifestations between the two. Conclusion: L-GCTS and FTS are very similar in clinical features, disease course, predilection site, predilection age, tumor size, and tumor appearance. Imaging examination methods are difficult to distinguish between the two before surgery. The differentiation between the two mainly relies on histopathology and immunohistochemistry, and the two also exhibit different molecular genetics. Although both L-GCTS and FTS are benign tumors, their recurrence rates and other prognostic factors are different. Therefore, it is necessary to clearly distinguish between the two.

title: Current Management of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) ~A Proposal for Early-stage PSC~.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic, progressive cholangiopathy characterized by inflammation and fibrosis of intrahepatic and/or extrahepatic bile ducts. Its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood, and liver transplantation is currently the only curative treatment available. The diagnosis remains challenging, and no disease-specific biomarkers have been established. Recently, anti-integrin αvβ6 antibodies have emerged as promising serological biomarkers with high specificity for PSC. Advances in imaging modalities, including magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography and peroral cholangioscopy, have improved diagnostic accuracy for PSC. Although various therapeutic approaches have been investigated, no treatment has been shown to improve the long-term outcomes. Microbiota-targeted therapies represent a promising emerging strategy. The clinical course of PSC, particularly in its early stages, is poorly defined. We propose a definition of early stage PSC consisting of two subtypes: small-duct PSC without liver fibrosis and large-duct PSC without cholestatic enzyme elevation or biliary strictures. Early intervention at this stage may improve the prognosis, thus highlighting the need for further validation.

title: Long-term Prognostic Value of Stress Phase Entropy for Predicting Major Cardiac Events in Patients with Known or Suspected Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: Objective This retrospective study aimed to investigate the long-term prognostic value and risk stratification in Japanese patients with known or suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) using poststress phase entropy, an index of left ventricular (LV) dyssynchrony.Methods The patients were followed up for six years to confirm their prognosis. The composite endpoint was the onset of major cardiac events (MCEs), including cardiac death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and severe heart failure requiring hospitalization. Poststress phase standard deviation (SD), bandwidth, and entropy were calculated using a phase analysis with the Heart Risk View-F software program.Patients The study included 2,421 patients with known or suspected CAD who underwent rest 201 Tl and stress 99 m Tc-tetrofosmin electrocardiogram-gated (ECG)-gated single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI).Results During the follow-up, 293 patients (13%) experienced MCEs. A multivariate analysis showed that age, the summed difference score, estimated glomerular filtration rate, stress LV ejection fraction (EF), and stress entropy were independent predictors of MCEs. A Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significant risk stratification between each group in the stress phase entropy tertiles. The global chi-squared value predicting MCE onset was significantly improved in the model with the summed stress score and stress LVEF plus entropy, but it was comparable in the model with added bandwidth or phase SD.Conclusion Stress phase entropy derived from ECG-gated SPECT MPI was a strong long-term predictor of MCEs in Japanese patients with CAD (known or suspected) and it is considered to be the most useful left ventricular dyssynchrony index to improve risk stratification over prediction by perfusion and LVEF assessment alone.

title: Role of EBUS-IFB in Providing High-quality Pathological Samples for a Sarcoidosis Diagnosis.
abstract: Objective Although endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) is the standard procedure for diagnosing mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy, its diagnostic yield for sarcoidosis remains suboptimal due to nodal fibrosis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided intranodal forceps biopsy (EBUS-IFB) has emerged as a promising adjunctive technique; however, concerns remain regarding the potential for crush artifacts when using mini-forceps. This study aimed to evaluate the histological specimen quality, diagnostic utility, and safety of EBUS-IFB in patients with suspected sarcoidosis in a single institution.Methods We retrospectively analyzed 11 consecutive patients with suspected sarcoidosis who underwent EBUS-IFB after EBUS-TBNA at a single center. We assessed the specimen quality, diagnostic yield, and safety. Two pathologists independently evaluated the specimens using a validated scoring system focusing on the amount of cellular material, background blood, degree of cellular degeneration and trauma, and retention of normal architecture.Results EBUS-IFB yielded significantly higher-quality specimens than EBUS-TBNA (median total score, 7.0 vs. 4.0; p = 0.01). Notably, EBUS-IFB specimens demonstrated well-preserved tissue architecture without significant crush artifacts and significantly less blood contamination (p = 0.006). The overall diagnostic yield was 81.8% (9 of 11), and definitive diagnoses of sarcoidosis were obtained by EBUS-IFB alone in six cases. No procedure-related complications were noted.Conclusions Despite concerns regarding crush artifacts, EBUS-IFB provides high-quality, structurally intact histological specimens with minimal blood contamination compared to EBUS-TB. EBUS-IFB is a safe and effective adjunctive modality that successfully compensates for the limitations of fine-needle aspiration in sampling fibrotic lymph nodes.

title: Pulmonary Inflammatory Myofibroblastic Tumor Mimicking Septic Pulmonary Embolism Following a Dental Infection.
abstract: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumors are rare mesenchymal neoplasms that may mimic infections. A 67-year-old man developed a persistent fever after dental extraction. Chest computed tomography revealed multiple bilateral peripheral pulmonary nodules with feeding vessel signs, suggesting a septic pulmonary embolism. Despite intravenous antibiotics, his fever persisted, and blood cultures remained negative. A video-assisted thoracoscopic lung biopsy revealed spindle cell proliferation with inflammatory infiltrates. The patient's condition deteriorated rapidly, and he developed multi-organ failure and died on hospital day 27. A subsequent immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated ALK positivity, confirming the diagnosis of an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor. An early tissue diagnosis is important when a presumed infection fails to respond to treatment.

title: AI Agents for Multimodal Oncology Diagnosis: Toward Transparent and Traceable Clinical Decision Support.
abstract: Cancer diagnosis depends on data from radiology, digital pathology, molecular profiling, laboratory testing, and longitudinal clinical records. AI performs well in selected tasks, but most systems remain narrow and disconnected from the iterative reasoning required in oncology. This Viewpoint defines an AI agent as a feedback-driven system that maintains task state, selects among governed tools, observes results, and revises its plan under explicit safety constraints. This definition separates agents from multimodal foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, and fixed workflow automation. We organize the discussion across multimodal data collection, preprocessing, fusion and representation learning, and diagnostic decision support. We distinguished agent-level evidence, component- or infrastructure-level evidence, and prospective propositions throughout. Clinical translation will require resilient failure handling, guideline version control, prospective evaluation, computational and workflow feasibility, and clinician authority over final decisions. The near-term opportunity is therefore transparent and traceable clinical decision support rather than autonomous cancer diagnosis.

title: Automated Renal Tumor Segmentation in Computed Tomography Images Using a Global Attention-Based DeepLabV3+ Model: Algorithm Development and Validation.
abstract: Background The rising global incidence of renal tumors necessitates precise diagnostic interventions. Accurate segmentation of computed tomography (CT) scans is essential for nephron-sparing surgery and radiotherapy. However, conventional manual delineation is labor-intensive and prone to significant interobserver variability due to tumor morphological heterogeneity. There is an urgent clinical demand for robust, automated segmentation solutions. Objective This study aims to develop and validate GAM-DeepLabV3+, an automated framework designed to address boundary ambiguity and high false-positive rates in complex renal imaging scenarios. Methods We propose an optimized encoder-decoder architecture specifically tailored for renal mass detection. The framework incorporates three key innovations: (1) a lightweight MobileNetV2 backbone to minimize computational overhead for clinical deployment; (2) an Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module to capture multiscale contextual information; and (3) a Global Attention Mechanism (GAM) in the decoder to enhance channel-spatial interactions, thereby refining boundary delineation by suppressing background noise. The model was rigorously evaluated on a private clinical dataset (n=218) and the KiTS19 benchmark (n=210). Results GAM-DeepLabV3+ consistently outperformed state-of-the-art baselines. On the private dataset, the model achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.939 (SD 0.008), significantly surpassing feature pyramid network (FPN; mean 0.893, SD 0.008; P <.001) and no-new-Net (nnU-Net; 2D, custom; mean 0.908, SD 0.013; P <.001). It also achieved a mean 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 1.485 (SD 0.522) pixels. On the KiTS19 dataset, it maintained a mean robust DSC of 0.928 (SD 0.006). To facilitate clinical translation, a demonstration-only online platform was developed. Conclusions The GAM-DeepLabV3+ framework provides an accurate, efficient, and fully automated solution for renal tumor segmentation. By overcoming boundary ambiguity and optimizing feature fusion, this approach shows potential as a decision-support aid, pending future validation with 3D reconstruction.

title: Radiographic assessment and orthodontic intervention effects on orthodontically induced root resorption: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials.
abstract: The relative contribution of radiographic methods and characteristics of the orthodontic intervention to orthodontically induced root resorption (OIRR) remains unknown. The aims of this systematic review and meta-analysis were to (1) estimate the pooled OIRR effect across orthodontic intervention versus comparator contrasts, (2) compare pooled estimates by radiographic method (2D [two-dimensional] vs. 3D/CBCT [three-dimensional/cone-beam computed tomography]), and (3) explore whether force mechanics (intrusive versus nonintrusive) modified OIRR magnitude. Seven randomized controlled trials and one prospective study (January 2010-October 2025) were included. Only OIRR was the outcome, reported as correlation coefficients (r). The primary analysis combined within-study intervention-versus-comparator estimates. Subgroup analysis of 2D versus 3D/CBCT imaging was prespecified, whereas post-hoc analysis of intrusive versus nonintrusive mechanics was performed. The pooled analysis for the primary outcome showed a small, nonsignificant OIRR effect (r = 0.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.12 to 0.27; p = 0.372) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 84.0%). Radiographic method did not change the pooled estimates significantly (p = 0.331). Force-mechanics analysis showed that intrusive mechanics was related to significantly higher root resorption than nonintrusive mechanics (r = 0.40; 95% CI = 0.15 to 0.65 versus r = -0.03; 95% CI = -0.16 to 0.10; p < 0.001). This accounted for 87.1% of the between-study variance. The average orthodontic intervention effect on OIRR was small and not significant; however, the OIRR magnitude was strongly affected by force mechanics, particularly by intrusive forces. There was no significant difference in pooled estimates by radiographic method; however, 3D/CBCT provides superior volumetric quantification and should be used judiciously according ALARA (as low as reasonably achievable) principles.

title: A multifunctional Fe 3 O 4 @Au-HPG-Glc theranostic platform for MRI/fluorescence-guided photothermal ablation of osteosarcoma.
abstract: Background The clinical management of osteosarcoma is challenged by its aggressive growth and deep anatomical location. Photothermal therapy offers a minimally invasive approach through localized thermal ablation, but its effectiveness is constrained by poor tissue penetration and inaccurate targeting of deep tumors without real-time guidance. Methods We synthesized flower-like Fe 3 O 4 @Au nanoparticles coated with hyperbranched polyglycerol (HPG) and conjugated with glucose (Glc) (Fe 3 O 4 @Au-HPG-Glc). In an osteosarcoma mouse model, the photothermal efficacy of the nanoprobes was evaluated by comparing two groups: the control group receiving phosphate-buffered saline plus laser irradiation (phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) + Laser) and the treatment group receiving Fe 3 O 4 @Au-HPG-Glc nanoprobes plus laser irradiation (NPs + Laser). Intratumoral temperature was monitored by infrared thermography, with longitudinal tracking of tumor volume and body weight. Major organs were examined by H&E staining. Tumor accumulation was assessed via whole-body fluorescence and T 2 -weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); pharmacokinetics and biodistribution were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Results The NPs + Laser regimen produced rapid intratumoral heating during the 0-4 min irradiation window and significantly delayed tumor growth compared with the PBS + Laser control group, with stable body weight and no overt organ lesions on H&E staining. Whole-body fluorescence and T 2 -weighted MRI confirmed tumor-site accumulation of the nanoprobes. ICP-MS-based pharmacokinetic and biodistribution analyses provided quantitative exposure context, including systemic clearance, reticuloendothelial system capture, and measurable tumor uptake. Together, these data facilitated interpretation of the subsequent photothermal response. Discussion Flower-like Fe 3 O 4 @Au-HPG-Glc enables image-guided photothermal treatment in an osteosarcoma model, supported by quantitative pharmacokinetic and biodistribution measurements and an acceptable short-course safety profile. This work establishes a clear imaging-exposure-response relationship and provides a strong foundation for further optimization of magnetic-optical combination strategies in precision cancer therapy.

title: Prognostic value of soluble ST2 in cardiac magnetic resonance defined myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries.
abstract: Background Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an essential role in identifying the underlying etiology of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). However, risk stratification in patients with CMR-confirmed MINOCA remains insufficiently defined. Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2), a biomarker related to myocardial fibrosis and adverse cardiac remodeling, may provide additional prognostic information in this population. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of sST2 in patients with CMR-confirmed MINOCA. Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients suspected of MI who underwent coronary angiography and completed CMR during hospitalization. MACE included all-cause death, recurrent MI, stroke, heart failure, arrhythmia, and angina pectoris. MINOCA was defined by evidence of ischemia or infarction on CMR. sST2 was tested using an immunoassay kit according to the protocol during hospitalization. Results A total of 97 patients with CMR-confirmed MINOCA were included. During a median follow-up of 24.2 months, 33 patients experienced MACE. Patients with MACE had significantly higher sST2 levels and worse CMR parameters, including lower left ventricular ejection fraction, greater late gadolinium enhancement extent, larger left ventricular end-systolic volume index, and impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS). Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that sST2 (HR 1.010, 95% CI 1.003-1.017, P = 0.005) and GLS (HR 0.864, 95% CI 0.780-0.956, P = 0.005) were independently associated with MACE. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate predictive performance for sST2, with an area under the curve of 0.696. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients with sST2 ≥ 36.95 ng/mL had a significantly higher risk of MACE. Conclusions Elevated sST2 is independently associated with adverse outcomes in patients with CMR-confirmed MINOCA. sST2 may serve as a practical biomarker for risk stratification in this population.

Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate predictive performance for sST2, with an area under the curve of 0.696. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients with sST2 ≥ 36.95 ng/mL had a significantly higher risk of MACE.

Conclusions

Elevated sST2 is independently associated with adverse outcomes in patients with CMR-confirmed MINOCA. sST2 may serve as a practical biomarker for risk stratification in this population.

title: Integration of MRI radiomics with immune profiling to predict response to CDK6 inhibitors in high-grade glioma.
abstract: Background Predictive biomarkers are needed to identify patients with high-grade glioma who benefit from cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6) inhibition. We hypothesized that an integrated Radiomics-Immune Score (R/I-Score), combining MRI-derived tumor heterogeneity with peripheral immune profiling, would predict progression-free survival (PFS) benefit from CDK6 inhibitor-containing therapy (CDK6i). Methods We conducted a two-center, retrospective cohort study utilizing longitudinal data from departmental neuro-oncology registries. The final study population comprised 116 adult patients with measurable disease who had undergone baseline contrast-enhanced MRI within 21 days prior to treatment initiation. To ensure methodological rigor and internal consistency, we adopted a two-stage study design. In the first stage (Biological Modeling), the total cohort ( N = 116) was partitioned into a training set ( n = 81) and an independent testing set ( n = 35) to develop and validate the R/I-Score. In the second stage (Clinical Validation), we addressed the selection bias inherent in observational data by performing 1:2 Propensity Score Matching (PSM). This yielded a balanced analytical cohort of 108 patients (36 treated with CDK6i and 72 concurrent contro\ls). The primary endpoint was the treatment-by-biomarker interaction for progression-free survival (PFS), specifically assessing the R/I-Score's ability to stratify therapeutic responders. Results In the overall matched cohort ( N = 108), patients treated with CDK6i exhibited numerical but statistically non-significant trends toward improved efficacy compared to concurrent controls in terms of median PFS (4.8 vs . 3.5 months; HR 0.72, P = 0.091), objective response rate (19.4% vs . 9.7%; P = 0.180), and disease control rate (44.4% vs . 30.6%; P = 0.165). The Combined R/I-Clinical Model demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance in the independent testing cohort ( N = 108), achieving a Treatment-Effect AUC of 0.97 and excellent calibration. In the PSM efficacy analysis, the R/I-Score successfully identified a distinct responder subpopulation: patients with a High R/I-Score derived significant survival benefit from CDK6i compared to concurrent controls (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.25-0.91; P = 0.008), whereas those with a Low R/I-Score did not (HR 1.05; 95% CI 0.58-1.92). The interaction between the R/I-Score and treatment was statistically significant ( P interaction = 0.012). Furthermore, High R/I-Score patients achieved superior objective response rates (33.3% vs. 5.6%) and sustained treatment duration (median 6 vs. 3 cycles) without increased toxicity (Grade ≥3 AEs: P >0.05). Biological interpretability analysis revealed that the score was driven by tumor morphological complexity and NK/CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Conclusions The multi-modal R/I-Score serves as a robust, non-invasive predictive biomarker for CDK6i therapy in GBM. By selecting patients based on specific radiomic-immune phenotypes, this tool facilitates precision oncology, maximizing therapeutic efficacy while avoiding futile treatment in non-responders.

title: Progression of coronary artery calcification in chronic kidney disease: nonlinear associations with serum magnesium and parathyroid hormone.
abstract: Introduction Coronary artery calcification (CAC) progresses rapidly in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but its trajectories across stages and nonlinear relationships with serum magnesium and parathyroid hormone (PTH) remain unclear. Methods We evaluated 800 CKD patients stratified into four groups (stages 1-2, 3, 4-5, and dialysis) over a median follow-up of 20.5 months using serial chest CT scans. Linear mixed-effects models, restricted cubic splines, and LASSO regression were applied to analyze trajectories, nonlinear relationships, and construct a predictive model. Results The annualized rate of CAC progression increased significantly with advancing CKD stages (8.5%, 13.2%, 22.8%, and 29.5%/year, respectively; P < 0.001). Serum magnesium exhibited an L-shaped nonlinear relationship with rapid CAC progression (inflection point: 0.82 mmol/L), while PTH showed a J-shaped relationship (inflection point: 120 pg/mL). Uric acid was linearly and positively correlated. A 7-factor LASSO-derived prognostic model demonstrated robust performance, yielding a C-statistic of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.772-0.832) and good calibration. Conclusion In conclusion, CAC progression accelerates as renal function declines, peaking in dialysis patients. Low magnesium (<0.82 mmol/L) and high PTH (120 pg/mL) are key nonlinear risk factors. The resulting predictive model provides clinical utility for stratified cardiovascular risk management.

title: Neuronavigation-guided precise resection versus conventional glioma surgery: a meta-analysis of clinical outcomes.
abstract: Background Neuronavigational surgery has become a cutting-edge technique that improves surgical accuracy, increases tumor excision rates, and preserves neurological function in glioma patients. Aim This meta-analysis was conducted to assess the efficacy of neuronavigational and advanced imaging-assisted surgery compared to traditional glioma surgery. Methods In total, 30 articles published between 2006 and 2026, including randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, retrospective cohort studies, and case series, were evaluated. The intervention involved intraoperative MRI (iMRI), ultrasound-guided navigation, functional neuronavigation, and other advanced navigational technologies. Meta-analysis was carried out using random effects models with inverse variance to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), I 2 and τ 2 measures of heterogeneity, and publication bias using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. The risk of bias was assessed through the Cochrane RoB 2 for 7 randomized controlled trials and ROBINS-I for 23 observational studies. Results Overall analysis demonstrated significant improvement with neuronavigation-guided surgery (OR = 2.37, 95% CI: 2.05-2.74, p < 0.05; I 2 = 22.8%). Subgroup analyses showed significant benefits for iMRI-guided surgery (OR = 2.49, 95% CI: 1.92-3.23, z = 6.88, I 2 = 22.6%, τ 2 = 0.0428, p = 0.2286), ultrasound-based navigation (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.47-2.66, z = 4.50, I 2 = 4.9%, τ 2 = 0.0084, p = 0.3685), functional neuronavigation (OR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.59-2.80, z = 5.17, I 2 = 0%), advanced navigation technologies (OR = 2.33, 95% CI: 1.67-3.25, z = 4.99, I 2 = 16.4%), and other specialized techniques (OR = 2.16, 95% CI: 1.63-2.86, z = 5.34, I 2 = 8.3%). Leave-one-out analysis confirmed the stability of the pooled effect, with minimal changes after exclusion of individual studies. Conclusion Neuronavigation-based and image-enhanced surgical procedures can significantly improve glioma surgery outcomes, with low heterogeneity and strong pooled effects. Large-scale multicenter studies are needed in order to prove their efficacy in the long term.

title: Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging in stroke: current applications, limitations, and future directions.
abstract: Stroke is currently one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide among neurological diseases. Although traditional imaging techniques can clearly delineate lesion extent and hemorrhagic patterns, they are limited in quantifying microscopic structural changes and repair processes in early-stage brain tissue damage. Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (NODDI), an advanced diffusion-weighted MRI technique, enables accurate, non-invasive quantification of post-stroke microstructural changes in brain tissue. NODDI objectively quantifies neurite damage and remodeling, providing crucial imaging evidence for stroke severity, prognosis, and rehabilitation outcome evaluation. This review critically synthesizes NODDI's biophysical principles, evaluates its expanding applications in both ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke-highlighting recent advancements in modeling and clinical translation-discusses persistent limitations, and proposes a roadmap for future research to maximize its clinical utility and address current challenges. Importantly, this review focuses exclusively on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based techniques and does not cover non-MRI modalities such as computed tomography (CT) or positron emission tomography (PET). Notably, post-stroke depression (PSD) affects approximately one-third of stroke survivors and represents a major neuropsychiatric complication that impedes functional recovery and reduces quality of life. Emerging evidence demonstrates that NODDI-derived metrics-particularly ODI and ISO-can identify microstructural disruptions in emotion-related white matter pathways that are specific to PSD, offering potential neuroimaging biomarkers that surpass conventional DTI parameters. These findings position NODDI as a promising tool not only for stroke characterization but also for bridging the gap between focal brain injury and subsequent psychiatric manifestations.

title: Preoperative prediction of serosal invasion in gastric cancer using multiphase contrast-enhanced CT radiomics.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a radiomics-based model using multiphase contrast-enhanced CT for the preoperative prediction of serosal invasion in gastric cancer, and to evaluate whether the integration of clinical and CT morphological features could further improve predictive performance. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 183 patients with surgically confirmed gastric cancer. All patients underwent multiphase CT (arterial, venous, and delayed phases). Radiomic features were extracted from volumetric regions of interest (VOIs). After feature selection and radiomics model construction, a combined nomogram was developed incorporating independent clinical and imaging predictors. Models were evaluated in training and validation cohorts using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Results The arterial plus delayed (AP+DP) phase radiomics model demonstrated the best performance, with AUCs of 0.8256 and 0.8179 in the training and validation sets, respectively. Multivariate analysis identified serum CA724 levels and serosal stranding as independent predictors. The combined nomogram incorporating these factors and the radiomics signature achieved AUCs of 0.8626 and 0.8641 in the training and validation sets, respectively. A clinical model was also established, with AUCs of 0.7738 and 0.7654 for the training and validation sets. Conclusion A radiomics model based on AP+DP CT phases shows strong potential for predicting serosal invasion in GC.The integration of CA72-4 and serosal stranding further increased the AUC of the combined model. The combined model achieved a statistically significant improvement in AUC over the clinical model in the training set, providing a non-invasive tool to support preoperative decision making.

title: Case Report: MR-guided adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy for splenic metastases: a case series of technical feasibility and early clinical outcomes.
abstract: We present a case series of four patients with five splenic metastases treated with stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) using a 1.5-T Unity (Elekta AB, Stockholm, Sweden) magnetic resonance linear accelerator (MR-Linac). While SBRT is a standard of care for the treatment of oligometastatic disease, splenic SBRT is not well established due to its rarity. MRI-guided adaptive radiotherapy (MRgART) offers superior soft tissue visualization and the unique ability to adapt treatment plans in real time. In our series, splenic oligometastases originated from primary malignancies of melanoma, colorectal adenocarcinoma, and non-small-cell lung cancer. Prescription doses ranged from 40 to 50 Gy in five fractions, with gross tumor volumes between 2.4 and 22.7 cm 3 . At 12 months, the local control was 80%. One patient developed grade 2 lymphopenia without infection following two courses SBRT with a total mean spleen dose of 24.4 Gy. Our experience suggests that MRgART is a technically feasible, effective, and non-invasive treatment for splenic metastases, offering excellent disease control with an acceptable toxicity profile. However, the benefits of splenic SBRT should be balanced against the potential risk of hematological toxicity, and prophylactic vaccinations for hyposplenism should be considered for this patient population.

title: Case Report: rapid clinical complete response to Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab combined with radiotherapy and chemotherapy in a patient with MSS/pMMR locally advanced rectal cancer.
abstract: Objective To investigate the efficacy and safety of Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab, a PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, in combination with chemoradiotherapy for a patient with microsatellite stable/mismatch repair proficient (MSS/pMMR) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), and to analyze the mechanism of achieving short-term clinical complete response (cCR). Methods This case report presents a 61-year-old male with stage cT3N2aM0 IIIB MSS/pMMR rectal cancer. The patient received neoadjuvant therapy with Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab (300mg per dose) plus XELOX regimen chemotherapy and radiotherapy (45Gy/25F). Responses were regularly assessed via digital rectal examination, imaging, endoscopy, and pathology. Results After treatment, clinical complete response (cCR) was initially evidenced by MRI at week 12 and subsequently confirmed by endoscopic assessment combined with pathologic biopsy at week 20. No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events occurred. At the last follow-up in March 2026, no recurrence was observed. Conclusion This case suggests that Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab combined with chemoradiotherapy may induce rapid cCR in MSS/pMMR LARC, offering a promising organ-preserving strategy through immunotherapy. Further large-sample studies are warranted.

title: Internal jugular venous flow responses to graded lower body negative pressure: a sex-stratified analysis.
abstract: Background The internal jugular vein (IJV) is the primary pathway for cerebral venous drainage in the supine position. Although lower body negative pressure (LBNP) is widely used to simulate central hypovolemia, the dose-response relationship between graded LBNP and jugular venous flow, and potential sex differences therein, remain incompletely characterized. We hypothesized that graded LBNP would produce a progressive, dose-dependent reduction in jugular venous flow, and examined whether this response differed between sexes. Methods Forty-four healthy young adults (22 female, 22 male) underwent graded LBNP (-10 to -40 mmHg) in the supine position. IJV cross-sectional area and blood flow velocity were assessed using B-mode ultrasound and pulsed-wave Doppler at the mid-neck (J2 segment). Volumetric flow was calculated as the product of mean area and mean envelope velocity. Relative flow changes (normalized to individual supine baseline) were log-ratio transformed prior to analysis. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with state, sex, and their interaction as fixed effects. Results Female participants showed significant jugular venous flow reductions at LBNP30 and LBNP40 (bothp< 0.001); males showed significant reductions from LBNP20 onward (p ≤0.0004). The main effect of sex was not significant (p = 1.00), and no state× sex interaction reached significance across LBNP levels or during recovery. A non-significant trend toward a larger flow reduction in females at LBNP40 (p = 0.056) did not persist in a completers-only sensitivity analysis (p = 0.16). Baseline IJV cross-sectional area was larger in males (p = 0.031) but did not differ after indexing to body surface area (p = 0.23). Conclusion Graded LBNP induces a progressive, dose-dependent reduction in jugular venous flow from moderate levels onward. Despite sex differences in Systemic responses, the jugular venous flow response was broadly similar between females and males, and baseline morphological differences were largely Attributable to body size. These observations are consistent with jugular venous outflow during central hypovolemia being governed predominantly by mechanical factors, although the modest sample size and exploratory analyses warrant confirmation. These findings inform the physiological understanding of jugular venous responses to central hypovolemia and are relevant to spaceflight countermeasures.

title: Imaging-based development and validation of artificial intelligence models for lung adenocarcinoma precursor lesions and early lung adenocarcinoma presenting as pulmonary nodules.
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative assessment of pulmonary nodule invasiveness remains challenging. We developed an internally validated multimodal framework integrating CT representations from a frozen vision foundation model with clinical variables. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included 1,179 pathologically confirmed pulmonary nodules: 247 glandular precursor lesions comprising atypical adenomatous hyperplasia and adenocarcinoma in situ , and 932 invasive lesions comprising minimally invasive and invasive adenocarcinoma. CT volumes were resampled to 0.5-mm isotropic resolution and cropped into 64 × 64 × 64-voxel patches. Slice-level representations were extracted using a pretrained, frozen DINOv3 backbone and aggregated by a trainable Attention Probe. Encoded clinical variables and imaging representations were integrated through self-attention and bidirectional cross-attention, followed by neural classification and regression tree classification. Internal validation used a five-fold rotating train-validation-test procedure, with each fold serving once as the held-out test fold. Results The held-out test-fold AUCs were 0.848, 0.864, 0.867, 0.882, and 0.822, yielding a mean AUC of 0.8566. Pooled out-of-fold predictions produced an AUC of 0.847, accuracy of 0.809, sensitivity of 0.806, specificity of 0.822, and F1 score of 0.873. DINOv3 and NCART achieved the highest point-estimate AUCs among the evaluated feature extractors and classifiers, respectively, although most pairwise differences were not statistically significant. Intermediate fusion significantly outperformed the Gould score and the clinical-data-only model, but not the imaging-only or late-fusion models. In the prespecified secondary analysis, the model achieved an AUC of 0.780 for distinguishing adenocarcinoma in situ from atypical adenomatous hyperplasia. Conclusion The proposed framework achieved internally validated discrimination of pulmonary nodule invasiveness. External multicentre and prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: One patient with synchronous multiple primary colon cancers which is easy to miss: a case report.
abstract: Background Multiple primary colon cancer is a relatively rare type of colon cancer (CC), and it is even rarer to have endoscopic obstruction. Case summary A 70-year-old female patient was previously diagnosed with sigmoid colon cancer accompanied by endoscopic obstruction at an external hospital. Preoperative abdominal enhanced CT in our hospital revealed one segmental bowel wall thickening with intussusception, and two separate thickened lesions in the transverse colon. During the operation, it was found that the intestinal wall of sigmoid colon, the transverse colon near splenic flexure and the ascending colon were obviously thickened and stiff, and the lymph nodes at the root of inferior mesenteric artery, the ileocolic artery and middle colon artery were swollen. Finally, we performed laparoscopic sigmoidectomy, left hemicolectomy, and right hemicolectomy with mesenteric lymph node dissection and ileorectal anastomosis. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed that adenocarcinoma existed in sigmoid colon, transverse colon and ascending colon. Conclusion Intraoperative comprehensive exploration is critical for the management of obstructive colon cancer. For patients with incomplete preoperative colonoscopy caused by tumor-induced luminal obstruction, meticulous intraoperative assessment is essential to avoid missed diagnosis of synchronous multiple CC and optimize long-term oncological outcomes.

title: Non-Invasive Assessment of Tertiary Lymphoid Structure in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Based on Multi-Parameter Imaging: From Tumor Immunobiology to Immunotherapy Benefit Prediction.
abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are ectopic lymphoid aggregates within the intratumoral and peritumoral microenvironment. In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the presence of TLSs was closely associated with immunotherapy response and prognostic outcomes. However, TLSs exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity within tumors and biopsy, being invasive and prone to sampling bias, may cause inaccurate assessments. Multi-parametric imaging techniques based on computed tomography (CT)/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)CT/MRICT/MRI with the aid of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms could effectively integrate anatomical structures with functional metabolic information, quantifying and visualizing key pathological molecular features of tumor treatment response across multiple dimensions. This review summarizes the biological characteristics and clinical significance of TLSs in hepatocellular carcinoma. Furthermore, it focuses on the latest advances in non-invasive TLS assessment using multi-parametric imaging techniques, integrating these technologies with large-scale artificial intelligence models to explore their application value in prognosis prediction and immunotherapy benefit evaluation.
